subject: RFP: Implementation & Canary Cadence — Redwood Inference
messages:
From: Lisa Wu <lisa.wu@acmebank.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@acmebank.com>, procurement@acmebank.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Acme Bank RFP — Implementation & Migration Questionnaire

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. As part of our vendor selection we need a detailed implementation/migration questionnaire that covers timeline, integration steps, rollback/canary plan, and what evidence you can provide for SOC2/audit logs and KMS integration. A few specific items we need answered:

- High-level timeline for pilot -> canary -> full production (we expect 8–12 weeks but open to alternatives)
- Integration checklist (network, auth, data flows, prefix/KV cache warm-up)
- Canary cadence and circuit-breaker thresholds (what metrics trigger rollback)
- Dependencies on our side (firewall rules, IAM roles, test data scope)
- Evidence for logging/audit trails and retention policies
- Any data residency or region constraints for hosted vs private deployments

Can you return a filled questionnaire and a proposed schedule by end of the week? We may share the responses with our infrastructure and security reviewers.

Thanks,
Lisa Wu
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Bank
[lisa.wu@acmebank.com]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Wu <lisa.wu@acmebank.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@acmebank.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Bank RFP — Implementation & Migration Questionnaire

Lisa —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is our completed implementation questionnaire (redwood_implementation_questionnaire_v1.pdf). Below is a concise, pragmatic timeline and an outline of the canary cadence we recommend for banking production workloads. If that looks good we can map owners and lock dates.

High-level proposed timeline (10 weeks total):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff, access provisioning, and scope alignment (network allowlists, service accounts, KMS exchange)
- Week 2–3: Integration sprint — authentication, endpoint wiring, prefix/KV cache seeding with synthetic traffic
- Week 4–5: Pilot (staging with real data subset) — feature verification, performance baselining, SLO tuning
- Week 6: Canary Phase 1 — 1% production traffic, 48–72h observation window, automated rollback thresholds enabled
- Week 7: Canary Phase 2 — 10% traffic, additional checks (cost per token, end-to-end latency P95/P99)
- Week 8: Canary Phase 3 — 50% traffic, load validation and SLA verification
- Week 9–10: Full cutover and post-cutover monitoring (30-day stability window)

Canary controls & circuit-breakers (short):
- SLO degradation: if error rate > 0.5% for 15m or P99 latency > 2x baseline for 15m -> auto-fallback to previous model variant
- Cost guardrail: if cost per 1k tokens increases >25% over baseline during a canary window -> pause rollout and revert routing policy
- Data-quality: regression alerts on prompt-based eval set (we run nightly checks during canary) -> manual halt

Integration steps (summary):
- Network: allowlist Redwood egress IPs / enable VPC peering for Private deployment
- Auth: OIDC service account + mTLS where required; KMS/HSM key transfer for private deployments
- Data flows: ingestion pipeline for prompts and optional embeddings; clear contract for PII redaction
- Cache warming: seed KV cache with representative prefixes during Week 2–3 to reduce first-token latency

Attachments included: redwood_implementation_questionnaire_v1.pdf (answers + evidence links). We also have a draft canary runbook (canary_runbook_draft.xlsx) which Marcus will share with specific operational steps.

Proposed next steps: quick walkthrough (30–45m) with your infra and security leads early next week; after alignment we’ll lock the kickoff date.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_implementation_questionnaire_v1.pdf (12 KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

On Thu, Nov 26, 2026 at 10:02 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (see Stephanie's proposed timeline and questionnaire)

Lisa / team —

Adding some operational detail you can drop into your runbook; this is the material we've found most useful for regulated banking customers.

Canary cadence (detailed):
- Canary 1 (Week 6): 1% routing weight for 72 hours. Metrics to monitor live: error rate, P95/P99 latency, token throughput, model divergence score on seed prompts. Automated alarms with 2-tier actions (auto-fallback -> page on-call -> pause rollout).
- Canary 2 (Week 7): Move to 10% for 72 hours. Include cost telemetry and warm path testing (cold vs warm cache comparisons).
- Canary 3 (Week 8): 50% for 48–72 hours. Run batch stress tests to validate autoscaling policies and dedicated GPU pool behavior.

Operational checkpoints & runbook snippets (we will provide the spreadsheet):
- Pre-canary checklist: traffic shaping rules, test data ingestion, prefix cache seed script completed, smoke test pass
- During canary: automated weekly snapshot of audit logs + daily integrity check; validate KMS key rotation policy; verify that KV-cache hit ratio >= 85% after seeding window
- Post-canary: 7-day elevated monitoring, then 30-day stability window before SLA starts counting fully

Fallback options we recommend upfront:
- Route to a quantized lower-cost model variant if latency SLO violated but availability is OK (reduces cost and keeps app responsive)
- Region fallback: automatic routing to a secondary region (same model family) for region-level instability

Security/compliance notes:
- SOC2 artifacts: we will provide SOC2 Type II report redactions and a control mapping for all API interactions.
- Audit logs: token-level request logs, hashed identifiers, and configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days)
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM via API) for Private deployment; we can adapt to your procurement-required attestation process

We attached the initial runbook (canary_runbook_draft.xlsx) in case you want to edit operational steps. Happy to join the walkthrough — I’ll bring the on-call runbook and automation snippets.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Stephanie / Marcus —

Thanks — the questionnaire and proposed cadence look solid and address the core concerns from our infra and security teams. Two quick items from procurement/security:

2) Please include the SOC2 Type II redaction and the KMS attestation as a deliverable before the start of Canary 1. Procurement will also need a placeholder PO and the estimated monthly committed spend for the Dedicated option (we'll circulate PO once terms are agreed).

If you can share the shifted timeline and a 30m walkthrough slot next Tuesday (Dec 1) between 09:00–12:00 PT, we can get security and infra on the call and (hopefully) lock dates.

Appreciate the rapid response.

Best,
